jobs.title: Lead Care Manager
jobs.description:
**Join EA Family Services**

EA Family Services is seeking a dedicated and compassionate **Lead Care Manager (LCM)** to join our **Sacramento** team. In this role, you will provide Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and care coordination services to Medi\-Cal members, helping individuals overcome barriers to stability, health, and wellness.

We are looking for someone who is passionate about serving vulnerable populations, particularly justice\-involved individuals and those experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The ideal candidate is respectful, objective, organized, and committed to empowering others through person\-centered support.

**Bilingual English/Spanish candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.**

About the Population We Serve

This position requires experience working with the **justice\-involved population**. Justice\-involved lived experience refers to personal experience navigating the legal or criminal justice system, including direct interactions with courts, corrections, probation, parole, or related systems. Candidates with professional or lived experience supporting justice\-involved individuals are encouraged to apply.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) in Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, or a related social science field required
* Minimum of two years of experience in a social services, case management, or care coordination setting
* Experience serving justice\-involved individuals required
* Bilingual English/Spanish preferred
* Valid California Driver's License with a clean driving record
* Ability to pass:
* Department of Justice (DOJ) Clearance
* Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Clearance
* Child Abuse Central Index Clearance (CAIC)
* Health Screening and TB Clearance

**Essential Skills and Abilities**

* Understanding of human growth, development, and trauma\-informed care
* Interest in serving individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing instability
* Ability to maintain a respectful, objective, and non\-discriminatory approach
* Strong interpersonal, engagement, and advocacy skills
* Excellent verbal and written communication abilities
* Professional, mature, and responsible work ethic
* Friendly, outgoing, and community\-oriented personality
* Strong organizational and documentation skills

**Primary Responsibilities** 

**Care Coordination \& Case Management**

* Provide consultation, care coordination, and case management services to ECM participants.
* Collaborate with clients, family members, natural supports, and community partners to develop individualized care plans.
* Assist clients in establishing SMART goals and support progress toward achieving those goals.
* Monitor care plans, evaluate progress, and revise services as needed.

**Member Engagement \& Support**

* Maintain regular contact with assigned clients, including weekly outreach and monthly face\-to\-face visits, or more frequently when necessary.
* Transport participants when appropriate and assist with access to community resources and services.
* Manage a caseload of approximately 25 members, with the potential to support up to 50 members based on program needs.

**Collaboration \& Advocacy**

* Coordinate with medical providers, behavioral health professionals, social service agencies, housing providers, and other community partners.
* Maintain ongoing communication with multidisciplinary treatment teams to ensure comprehensive support.

**Documentation \& Compliance**

* Complete timely progress notes, case notes, quarterly reports, and other required program documentation.
* Administer the Adult Needs and Strengths Assessment (ANSA) at intake and every six months thereafter.
* Develop transition and discharge plans, including aftercare and follow\-up support.
* Monitor housing placements to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and standards.
* Follow all State and Federal regulations regarding confidentiality, mandated reporting, and client rights.

**Program Operations**

* Report any potentially harmful, illegal, or safety\-related concerns to management immediately.
* Participate in on\-call responsibilities as required to meet client needs.
* Use the designated communication system when communicating with members.
* Perform other duties as assigned by agency leadership.

**Why Join EA Family Services?**

EA Family Services is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening individuals, families, and communities throughout Northern California. We offer:

* Competitive pay
* Comprehensive health benefits
* Paid time off
* Retirement benefits
* Professional development opportunities
* Supportive team environment
* Meaningful work that changes lives

**EA Family Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE).**

**Apply today to make a lasting difference in the lives of individuals and families in your community.**

“Required to use the designated communication system when communicating with Members.”

Job Type: Full\-time

Pay: $25\.00 per hour

Benefits:

* 403(b)
* 403(b) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Must pass DOJ/FBI/CAIC clearances

jobs.description:
**Lead Care Manager (ECM Support Counselor)**
Join our team as an ECM Support Counselor and take part in transforming the way Medi\-Cal members with complex needs receive care and support.
As an ECM Support Counselor, you'll serve as the primary point of contact for Medi\-Cal members enrolled in Enhanced Care Management (ECM). You will conduct outreach research across healthcare, community\-based, and social\-service settings throughout the San Francisco Bay Area to identify opportunities for connecting with and enrolling new client\-members. You'll develop trusting relationships with members and provide comprehensive, individualized care management that addresses medical, behavioral health, and health\-related social needs.
Working primarily in the community, you'll coordinate with health care providers, social service agencies, community organizations, and other members of the care team to ensure members receive the right services at the right time.
This is a full\-time, benefited role with significant community\-based work. The position requires flexibility to meet members where they live and receive services, including homes, health care settings, community centers, and other community locations. The ideal candidate is compassionate, organized, has strong public speaking and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with individuals or community groups, comfortable working in community\-based settings, and culturally responsive and can support to individuals and families from diverse backgrounds.  


**About Alternative Family Services**
Alternative Family Services is a Foster Family, Adoption and Mental Health Agency that has been serving abused and neglected children in our community since 1973\. Our mission is to support vulnerable children and families in need of stability, safety, and well\-being in communities. We provide a wide range of foster, adoption, mental health and transition\-aged youth services in English and Spanish. We have eight locations throughout the Bay Area and over 200 employees. We celebrate diversity, equal opportunity, and excellence.  


**Responsibilities and What You’ll Do*** Build relationships with community\-based, social service, healthcare and other partner organizations throughout the San Francisco Bay Area to increase awareness of ECM services and generate new client\-member enrollment.
* Identify and engage with community\-based, social\-service or healthcare organizations to generate new client\-member enrollment and strengthen community partnerships
* Plan, coordinate and participate in community outreach events to increase awareness and enrolment of ECM services, foster relationships with prospective clients, and generate new client\-member enrollment
* Serve as the member’s primary point of contact, providing individualized and comprehensive care management; provide direct support services such as mentoring, skill\-building, coaching, tutoring, and crisis response.
* Develop person\-centered care plans in partnership with members, their families or support systems, and the care team
* Meet with client\-members in their homes and communities to assess needs, provide support, and help remove barriers to care
* Help client\-members navigate health care and social service systems and connect them to appropriate providers and community resources across multiple systems
* Coordinate referrals and follow up to ensure client\-members successfully access recommended services
* Maintain regular communication with health plans, providers, community\-based organizations, and other members of the interdisciplinary care team
* Advocate for members and help ensure their preferences, goals and needs remain central to their care
* Maintain accurate and timely documentation in accordance with organizational, Medi\-Cal, and health plan requirements
* Maintain confidentiality and compliance with HIPAA and applicable privacy standards
* Monitor member progress and update care plans as needs and circumstances change
* Participate in care team meetings, case consultations, and other activities designed to improve coordination and outcomes
* Respond appropriately to urgent member needs and help connect members to crisis or emergency resources when necessary

  

**Qualifications**
* Ability to obtain and maintain fingerprint and government and Agency required background clearances
* CPR/First Aid certification
* Valid California driver’s license with an acceptable driving record, auto insurance showing as an insured driver on the policy and vehicle registration
* A bachelor’s degree in a social science related field; or an associate degree in a social science related field and have at least six months experience in working with emotionally disturbed children or children who have a serious behavioral problem; or at least two years of experience working with emotionally disturbed children or children who have a serious behavioral problem, and who demonstrate a combination of education, skills, and experience
* Experience providing case management, care coordination, social services, behavioral health services, health care services, or related support to individuals with complex needs
* Experience as an outreach coordinator and comfortability with public speaking
* Knowledge of county and community resources and the ability to connect members to social service programs
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills
* Experience working with individuals experiencing complex medical, behavioral health, housing, food insecurity, or other social needs
* Ability to maintain accurate documentation and manage multiple cases, deadlines, and follow\-up activities
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary care team
* Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, cultural humility, and person\-centered care
* Able to interact with co\-workers, county representatives, and other treatment team member

Lutheran Social Services of Southern California was officially incorporated in 1946 as a 501(c)(3\) non\-profit social service agency. jobs.description:
**Why join Connections**

If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact, working in a mission\-driven environment, and helping redefine behavioral health crisis care, we invite you to join us at Connections Health Solutions. Together, we're saving lives and changing the face of behavioral health.


**A****bout** **Connections**



We're not just behavioral health people—we're crisis people. When individuals need support *now*, we provide immediate\-access behavioral health crisis care that stabilizes, supports, and connects people to the resources they need to continue their recovery.



Founded by emergency room psychiatrists, our physician\-led, data\-driven model is backed by more than 15 years of crisis care expertise. Recognized by SAMHSA and the National Council for Mental Wellbeing as a national best practice, we've delivered critical crisis care to thousands of people during some of the most challenging moments of their lives. Our mission is simple and unwavering: providing immediate care to people in crisis and connecting them to long\-term support within their community.


**About the RESET Center,** **operated** **by Connections**



Located in San Francisco's South of Market neighborhood, the RESET Center provides an alternative destination for individuals who are found to be publicly intoxicated (due to alcohol and/or drugs) and would otherwise be transported to the emergency department or jail.



In collaboration and partnership with local law enforcement and public health agencies, the RESET Center aims to effectively divert intoxicated individuals away from the criminal justice and/or healthcare systems to improve outcomes, reduce systemic burden, and support connection to needed resources within the community.

  


**Earn More with Shift Differentials**



Maximize your earnings with additional hourly pay:


* \+$2/hr \-\> Monday\-Thursday Nights
* \+$3/hr \-\> Friday\-Sunday Nights
* \+$2/hr \-\> Saturday\-Sunday Days


**What You'll Do:**  



The **Case Manager** at the RESET Center provides person\-centered care coordination, engagement, and discharge planning to individuals utilizing the sobering program. Working from a harm\-reduction and trauma\-informed approach, the CM supports participants in stabilizing safely, explores immediate needs, and connects them to ongoing services in the community.  



This role conducts brief screenings and assessments, engages in crisis de\-escalation when needed, and collaborates closely with community partners—including onsite Sheriff's staff, local law enforcement, emergency departments, and outpatient providers—to facilitate rapid discharge and seamless linkage to care. The CM ensures participants leave the program with clear next steps and access to resources that promote health, recovery, and stability.
* Welcome individuals with empathy, respect, and a non\-judgmental approach in a low\-barrier, trauma\-informed environment.
* Engage participants using motivational interviewing to identify needs, goals, and readiness for services.
* Conduct brief screenings and assessments to understand risk, safety, and resource needs.
* Provide education, encouragement, and practical support tailored to participant goals.
* Develop short\-term, accessible discharge plans for individuals staying between 4–24 hours.
* Coordinate referrals and warm handoffs to community resources including:
	+ Substance use treatment (outpatient, detox, MAT)
	+ Managed alcohol programs
	+ Mental health providers
	+ Shelters, crisis housing, and social services
	+ Hospital or emergency care when clinically appropriate
* Support crisis de\-escalation and conflict intervention in collaboration with the care team.
* Document timely and accurate services entries in Epic to support care coordination, safety, and communication.
* Maintain collaborative relationships with law enforcement, public health partners, and community agencies.
* Complete required RESET Center trainings.
* Perform all other duties as assigned.


**What You'll Bring:**
* 1\-3 years of experience in harm reduction, crisis services, behavioral health, or related community care settings
* High School diploma or equivalent
* Experience supporting law enforcement diversion or working alongside first responders, emergency departments, or criminal\-legal partners
* Must obtain Overdose Prevention and Narcan Administration training within 30 days of hire
* Basic computer literacy, including the ability to document in an electronic health record (EHR)
* Ability to obtain and accurately record vital signs

WestCoast Children's Clinic, located in Oakland, California, is a non\-profit community psychology clinic that provides mental health services to Bay Area children, youth and families. ***Working at WestCoast Children's Clinic means being part of an organization that is client\-centered, trauma\-informed, collaborative, and committed to justice and equity.***

**Position Details**


**Title**: Bilingual C\-Change Case Manager


**Classification**: Regular Full Time (1\.0 FTE), Non\-exempt (Hourly)


**Location**: Oakland, CA / Hybrid (availability to provide client services in\-person and complete documentation remotely)


**Regular Work Schedule**: Full time, M\-F


**Compensation:**


* $34\.37 per hour (inclusive of 10% Spanish language differential)


The **Bilingual (Spanish) C\-Change Case Manager** works in collaboration with WestCoast clinicians and parents, social workers, probation officers, teachers, and other adults in youths' lives to provide advocacy and linkage to support clients' mental functioning. These services may include coordinating with education and vocational programs, housing, primary health, psychiatry, benefits and other independent living skills services. The C\-Change Case Manager must have strong advocacy skills, demonstrate flexibility, utilize a strengths\-based approach, and have demonstrated experience working with high needs youth.


**How the C\-Change Case Manager makes an impact:**


* Provides advocacy, targeted case management, and community based rehabilitation services to transition\-age youth.
* Assists youth in identifying and utilizing community services and resources to address their needs, including: housing, medical/physical health, education, employment, independent living skills, advocacy, placement stability, and age\-appropriate enrichment activities in Alameda and SF county.
* Provide risk assessments, crisis intervention, stabilization, safety plans, and drop\-in counseling (as needed).
* Connects youth with legal representation, as needed and appropriate, and supports youth in court appearances.
* Provides psycho\-education about sexual exploitation and advocacy services for clients.
* Assists youth with accessing SSI and/or regional center services, appropriate housing resources including acute and structured residential treatment options as appropriate.
* Follow up with youth when incarcerated or hospitalized and transitioning to placements.
* Assists youth with obtaining and keeping Medi\-Cal.
* Complies with policies, procedures, documentation and paperwork for EPSDT Medi\-Cal billing and meets billing requirements as set by the agency.
* Demonstrates professional and ethical conduct at all times as a representative of the WestCoast community.
* Provides Enhanced Care Management (ECM) services
* Provides services in the community, for which travel by car is necessary.


**Key Qualifications:**


* At least 2\+ years of experience working with systems involved youth.
* Bachelor's degree in Psychology, Criminal Justice, Social Work, or a related field preferred.
* Bilingual in English and Spanish **(required)\***
* Experience providing case management and rehabilitation services.
* Demonstrated experience working with adolescents with dual diagnosis and high mental health needs and/or Sexually Exploited Minors.
* Knowledge of Alameda and SF County community resources for TAY youth.
* Experience working either in the community or in a variety of settings: homes, schools, neighborhoods, other agencies, etc.
* Experience in working with diverse communities.
* Ability to work with clients who have complex traumatic histories and other attachment difficulties.
* Ability to travel by car to meet with clients, generally within a 90 mile radius of WCC's Oakland office. Alternative forms of transportation may be accommodated based on the needs of the program and clients. Employees must have a clean CA DMV record. When driving for WCC, current vehicle insurance is required.


**Competencies:**


* Case management skill – assessment/evaluation, crisis intervention, ability to use supervision effectively, ethical and legal responsibilities, high quality documentation.
* Cultural humility \- knowledge of issues of race, class and ethnicity.
* Efficiency and time management \- ability to be well\-organized.

* Knowledge of or ability to learn Medi\-Cal reimbursement procedures and billing.

Final candidates will be required to complete an ALTA Language Proficiency Test administered by WestCoast Children's Clinic and must achieve a **minimum score of Level 9 (Advanced)** to qualify for the position.

As a catalyst for equity, the Program Manager will focus on being a key contributor toward the success and progress of the Santa Cruz County Health Workforce Council. Some key duties and responsibilities for this role include:  

**Core Functions:**
* Build and maintain cross\-sector partnerships with healthcare employers, education partners, workforce agencies, community organizations, and regional stakeholders across Santa Cruz County and the Central Coast.

* Track healthcare workforce policies, funding opportunities, and emerging workforce development practices to inform program and regional strategy.
* Support and regularly attend HIP convenings, including biweekly staff meetings, the HIP Council, Santa Cruz County Health Workforce Council, and Annual Board Meeting.

**Assigned Program Functions:**

* Support employer engagement and align workforce activities with regional hiring needs, educational capacity, and community priorities.

* Support efforts to secure sponsorships, shared investments, partner contributions, and other resources that strengthen the regional workforce collaborative.


  

**Qualifications**:

* Minimum three years of project/program management experience of high complexity in healthcare and/or an equivalent combination of graduate education and experience.

**Compensation and Classification**
HIP is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation practices. To support consistency and equity in our hiring process, we do not negotiate starting salaries. Compensation is determined based on the position’s classification, scope, and responsibilities.
